info.title: Tack API
info.description: REST + WebSocket API for Tack, a lightweight, workflow-agnostic project-management tool. This contract is generated from the Rust handlers and domain models; it is the single source of truth for the wire format. Every failing response, including one for a request the server could not read, shares the `{ "error": { "status", "code", "message", "retryable", "request_id", "details" } }` envelope; a caller branches on `code`, never on `message`.

post.summary: Resolve a pending decision with an operator-supplied answer
post.description: Operator-only, and more tightly scoped than the rest of the operator surface. Authenticates via the `x-tack-principal` header alone — this route never reads `Authorization` at all, so a valid runner bearer credential (even one issued for this exact attempt) cannot reach it; `handlers::decisions`'s own tests (`self_resolution_is_denied_*`) prove a runner credential carries zero privilege here even when presented. A runner may raise a decision and poll for its resolution (`POST .../decisions`, `POST .../decisions/poll`, both under `runner-protocol-v1`) but never resolve one itself. Idempotent: replaying the identical `answer` for an already-resolved decision returns the prior resolution (`replayed: true`) rather than erroring; a *different* `answer` is a 409 idempotency_conflict. A decision past its `expires_at` can never be resolved (409 decision_expired) — including one that transitions from `pending` to `expired` lazily on this very call, which still refuses the submitted answer. This route never writes an item's status, directly or indirectly (see `handlers::decisions`'s "No item-status mapping" section).

parameters.name: attempt_id
parameters.description: Attempt ID the decision belongs to (opaque)

parameters.name: decision_id
parameters.description: Decision ID, scoped to `attempt_id`: a decision_id that exists but belongs to a different attempt resolves as 404 not_found, indistinguishable from one that never existed at all — an attacker guessing another attempt's decision_id learns nothing.

parameters.name: x-tack-decision-token
parameters.description: TACK_EXECUTION_DECISION_TOKEN — a second, independent operator credential *on top of* the ordinary operator auth every other `/api` route uses (never a substitute for it). Fail-closed: every call is rejected with 403 whenever the server has not configured TACK_EXECUTION_DECISION_TOKEN at all — there is no "no secret configured, allow everything" fallback the way the plain Bearer gate has for an unset TACK_API_TOKEN.

requestBody.description: The operator's answer to this pending decision.

200.description: Decision resolved — either a fresh write or a byte-identical idempotent replay of one (`replayed` distinguishes the two).

400.description: invalid_request (missing/malformed answer, or answer.option_id is not one of this decision's own recorded options)

401.description: unauthorized — no x-tack-principal; a runner bearer credential never satisfies this, by construction

403.description: forbidden — x-tack-decision-token missing, unconfigured server-side, or mismatched (details.required_scope = "operator:decisions")

404.description: not_found — no decision exists for this exact (attempt_id, decision_id) pair

post.summary:
`POST /api/attempts/{attempt_id}/merge` — the Merge button. Merges the
attempt's pull request at its head commit, opening the pull request first when
it is missing; a refusal is a `409` carrying the reason, already recorded on
the item. When the pack recommends `reject`, or the change altered how the work is checked,
the person still decides, but writes why: the press is a `400` without a `reason`, and a merge that goes through is
kept as the attempt's accepting review, with that reason.

200.description: Merged; carries the merge commit's sha

400.description: invalid_request (the pack recommends reject, or the checks changed, and no reason was written)

409.description: conflict: the merge was held, the message says why

get.description: Operator-only (`x-tack-principal`); never reachable via a runner bearer credential — this route is mounted under the operator `/api` surface, not `runner-protocol-v1`. origin_ref.description: The run or thread it came from, when it came from one.

principal.description: Who proposed it: a principal label (`agent:<credential id>`, `operator:local`).

principal_name.description: The proposer's name when it is an agent credential.

rejection.description: Why a person turned the waiting operations down.

ChangeSetStatus.description: Where a change set stands. It is derived from its operations, never set on its own.

principal.description:
The principal that wrote it (`operator:...`, `agent:<credential id>`); `None` for a comment
written before callers were recorded, or by Tack itself.

ContinueResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/executions/{id}/continue` — a new request that follows the same
docket task the named run left stopped at its own step budget (Phase 87, decision 6), or an
idempotent replay of one already made.

CostByModel.description:
One model's tokens in the window. `tokens_in` and `tokens_out` are counted
tokens: the input the cache served is in `cache_read`, shown and not counted.

model.description: Absent for attempts that reported no model and asked for none.

usd.description: Absent without a rate card or when it does not list the model.

CostByTeam.description: One docket team's tokens in the window, counted as in [`CostByModel`].

usd.description: Absent without a rate card or when any of the team's models is unlisted.

agent_profile_id.description:
Omitted, the server picks one: run settings, the item's role, the project's
default, the implementer, and records which in `metadata.profile_source`.

autonomy.description:
The autonomy level a docket run is asked for: `L3`, `L4` or `L5`, sent to docket as it is.
Absent, docket decides from the team's profile; the project's level is never sent. `L3` is
"Run again at L3". Any other value, or a level for an agent other than docket, is
`invalid_request`.

budgets.description:
A run's limits. `tokens` absent: the profile's `limits.budgets.tokens`, else no limit;
`null`: no limit for this run even when the profile has one; a positive integer: that
many. `0`, a negative number or a non-number is refused (`invalid_request`, field
`budgets.tokens`). `cost_usd` was removed and is refused (`field_removed`).

from_run.description:
A previous execution request's id, to start this run from the work it kept instead of the
project's base commit. The server reads that request's newest evidence
(`actual_execution.git.branch`) and sets `metadata.rework_base` itself, the same key a
rework already reads — a request never carries the branch directly. A name that does not
exist is `not_found` (`details.reason = "from_run_not_found"`); one that belongs to
another project, or left no branch to continue from, is `unprocessable`
(`details.reason` is `"from_run_different_project"` or `"from_run_no_kept_work"`). Absent,
`metadata.rework_base` is read only when the caller set it directly, as before.

origin.description:
`mcp` marks a run an agent started through `tack mcp`: it is never merged
automatically or by a move to Done, only by the Merge button. Any other
value, or none, means a person started it.

permission_policy.description:
`tack_protocol::execution::PermissionPolicy` (`{tools, network,
approvals}`). `network` absent: the resolved profile's `tool_policy.network`, else
off; `true` or `false` is kept as sent. `approvals` is `"auto"` or `"ask"`; absent means
`"auto"`. `"ask"` is rejected at scheduling time for a runner whose
matched harness does not attest `decisions: supported`.

push_branch.description:
`false` declines the runner's branch push for this run. The runner's own
configuration decides whether a push exists; `true` never enables one.

repository_snapshot.description:
`tack_protocol::execution::RepositorySnapshot` (`{kind, remote,
base_revision, subdirectory}`). Omitted (or `{}`) the server fills it
from the item's project. An explicit one must name the project's own
repository (`details.reason = "repository_differs_from_project"`) and
may only add `base_revision` and `subdirectory`; a project with no code
is `invalid_request` (`details.reason = "project_has_no_code"`).

requested_harness_kind.description:
Omitted, the resolved profile's agent (`tool_policy.agent`), else the
project's default agent; with neither, `select_an_agent`.

requested_model.description:
The one model string the agent is asked to use, passed verbatim.
Absent, the project's default model applies when this run's agent is
the project's default agent; otherwise the agent chooses.

selector_kind.description:
`exact_runner` or `fleet`. Omitted (with `selector_id`), the agent profile's fleet,
else the only active runner; with neither, `select_where_this_runs`.

timeout_seconds.description: Absent: the profile's `limits.timeout_seconds`, else the default time limit.

verify.description:
`false` declines the runner's verifier for this run. The runner's own
configuration decides whether a verifier exists; `true` never enables one.

CreateExecutionResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/executions` — a newly created request or an
idempotent replay of an existing one (`replayed` distinguishes the two).

notice.description:
Present when the request named a setting that was removed: "ignored: the status is set by
a person".

state.description:
Always `"queued"` on success — a request enters the runner-v1
lifecycle (`docs/contracts/runner-v1/lifecycle-transitions.json`)
only once created.

artifact_id.description: The plan artifact the entries came from; absent means a file the person uploaded.

CreateOp.description:
One `create`: an entry of a plan (`docs/contracts/plan-v1`), with refs where the plan has
indexes.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria the item starts with.

depends_on.description: The items that block this one.

oneOf.description:
The item this one is a sub-item of; absent means a top-level item. A `New` parent is an
earlier operation.

profile_id.description: A profile, by id; it wins over `team`.

team.description: A team, by name; the one profile that names it does the item.

type.description: The item type, when the project has it; else the type of the set's anchor when that is work, else the default work type.

CreatePendingRunnerResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/runners/enrollment`. `enrollment_token` is
the raw, one-time secret — never persisted, never returned again by any
later response.

delivers.description: One line on what the profile delivers; empty or absent is no line.

fleet_id.description: The fleet a run with this profile goes to when it names no selector.

kind.description:
What the profile does: `implementer`, `reviewer`, `researcher`, `planner` or `custom`
(the default). It decides whether a run needs a repository.

warnings.description:
What the profile was saved with that deserves a second look, such as a method the team
names no member for.

oneOf.description:
Where the code is, settable at creation so a project never exists
without its folder in between two requests. Each absent field takes
the column's default (`none`, no repository, `local_branch`); the
handler validates `code_origin`/`repository` together exactly as a
`PATCH` does.

item_types.description: The project type's preset when absent.

depends_on.description: Indexes of entries in this list that block this one.

parent.description: The index of an earlier entry this one is a sub-item of; absent means a sub-item of the item.

profile_id.description:
A profile, by id: any profile, with a team or without, goes into the item's run settings.
It wins over `team`.

team.description: A team, by name; the one profile that names it goes into the item's run settings.

type.description: The item type, when the project has it; else the parent's when that is work, else the default work type.

credential_id.description:
When given, the thread reaches the projects this credential may read, and only that
credential (and the operator) may write in it.

profile.description: The agent profile whose runs are the thread's turns.

project_id.description: The project the thread's turns run in; with no credential, the only project it reaches.

credential_id.description:
When given, the events of the projects this credential may read count, and the
credential's own changes never wake the profile.

daily_cap.description: The most runs in a day (1 to 100).

project_id.description: The project the runs happen in; with no credential, the only project whose events count.

quiet_seconds.description: How long events stay quiet before the run starts, in seconds (0 to 3600).

unknown_profile.description:
The profile id that no profile has; the item's run settings name no profile from it, and
its `team` is still tried.

unknown_role.description: The role name the project does not have; the item has no role.

unknown_type.description: The type the project does not have; the item has its parent's type when that is work, else the default work type.

unresolved_team.description: The team that no profile, or more than one, names; the item's run settings name no profile.

CredentialState.description: What a credential is in now: only an active one authenticates.

CurrentStep.description: The step a task is inside.

cycle.description: How many times the task went back to an earlier step before this one; `0` on a first pass.

model.description: The model the step was planned on, which is not always the one that served it.

role.description: Who does the step, in the harness's own word for it, shown as data.

DecideMemoryRequest.description: What a person decides about a memory entry of a team.

reason.description: Why the entry is refused; required for a refusal, ignored for an approval.

DecisionAnswerSchema.description:
Schema-only mirror of the `answer` object `POST
.../decisions/{decision_id}/resolve` both accepts (`handlers::decisions::
validate_answer`) and echoes back on success. `option_id` must be a
non-empty string; when the decision's own `options` list is non-empty,
resolution also requires `option_id` to be one of them (checked
server-side, not expressible in this schema). `text` may be omitted,
`null`, or a string — never anything else.

DecisionResolvedBy.description:
The `resolved_by` of a settled decision: `{"kind": "operator", "subject_id": <principal>}`
for an operator's answer, `{"kind": "system", "subject_id": "expiry"}` for a decision that
passed its `expires_at`, `{"kind": "harness", "subject_id": <tool>}` for one the agent's own
tool took the answer to (`docket`). Not a closed enum on purpose: nothing in `docs/contracts/runner-v1/`
fixes this shape, so it stays an open two-field object.

DecisionSummary.description:
One `execution_decisions` row as an operator sees it — every column the
table carries, options/metadata/answer/resolved_by parsed out of their
raw JSON-string storage. `answer`/`resolved_by` stay untyped `Value`:
the wire shape they carry is documented by `handlers::decisions`'
`ResolveDecisionRequest`/`ResolveDecisionResponseSchema`, which this
module does not duplicate.

recommendation.description: The runner's recommended option: `{option_id, rationale, evidence_refs}`.

viewed_at.description: When an operator first opened this decision.

created_by.description:
Who made the link: `operator`, or the name of the agent credential; `None` when it was not
recorded.

as_of.description: The instant the digest was read at.

teams.description: The teams with work that has not ended, by name.

DomainSettings.description: One named area of the repository with its own level.

item_types.description: Item types the domain covers; empty means any.

merged.description: Read only: changes Tack merged by itself in this domain.

path_globs.description: Globs a change's every path must match (`**` crosses directories).

undone.description:
Read only: of those, how many were reverted or turned CI red (each one
took the domain down a level).

code.description:
Stable, machine-readable error code, on every error: a caller branches on *why* with it,
never by parsing `message`. The code decides `status`.

details.description:
What the error blames. `details.field` names the request field, path parameter or query
parameter that failed, when one did.

request_id.description:
The id of the request this answers, the one the client sent in `x-request-id` when it was
usable; the response carries it in the same header.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the same request can succeed (`StableErrorCode::retryable`).

status.description: HTTP status code, duplicated in the body for convenience.

field.description: The request field the error blames.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Structured error envelope returned by every failing endpoint — see
`crate::error::ApiError`. The body is always
`{ "error": { status, code, message, retryable, request_id, details } }`.

EventKind.description: The kinds of thing a trigger can wait for.

agent_profile_id.description: The profile the run was made with; null when the profile has since been deleted.

instructions.description: The composed prompt the agent is given, as stored with the request; null when absent.

limit.description: The run's token limit and who applies it.

never_started.description:
The run's newest attempt ended without ever starting work, the same flag the run list
carries (read through `tack_app::runs::run_facts`, the one rule).

prompt_template_sha.description:
The fingerprint (SHA-256, hex) of the prompt templates the instructions were composed with;
null for a run made before it was kept.

requested_harness_kind.description: The agent the run asked for; null when it left the choice to the computer.

oneOf.description:
What the verifier's pack for the run's newest attempt recommends (`merge`, `review` or
`reject`); null while that attempt has not succeeded, or when it left no readable pack.

waiting_behind.description:
The runs that hold every slot of the computers this request may run on, when no poll has
given a reason because those computers are full; empty otherwise. Read at read time.

waiting_reason.description: Why no runner has claimed this request yet, as a plain sentence; null once claimed.

waiting_since.description: When a runner's poll first found the request unclaimable; null once claimed.

ExecutionSummary.description:
One row of `GET /api/executions` / the `GET /api/executions/{id}`
detail. Deliberately five scalar columns today — attempt/event detail
is not carried here; it is available separately via `GET
/api/executions/{id}/attempts`.

agent_profile_id.description:
The profile the run was made with, so a screen finds the run's team and agent from the
run and not from the item's current setting; null when the profile has since been deleted.

oneOf.description:
The latest hop the run's newest attempt reported; null when the agent reports no hops
(every agent but docket) or the attempt has not reached its first one.

limit.description: The run's token limit and who applies it.

never_started.description:
The run's newest attempt ended without ever starting work: the computer refused it, or the
team's ceiling did. A screen reads "Not started" from this, never a failure of the work.

requested_harness_kind.description:
The agent the run asked for (`claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `docket`); null when it
left the choice to the computer.

oneOf.description:
What the verifier's pack for the run's newest attempt recommends (`merge`, `review` or
`reject`); null while that attempt has not succeeded, or when it left no readable pack.

waiting_behind.description:
The runs that hold every slot of the computers this request may run on, when no poll has
given a reason because those computers are full; empty otherwise. Read at read time.

waiting_reason.description: Why no runner has claimed this request yet, as a plain sentence; null once claimed.

waiting_since.description: When a runner's poll first found the request unclaimable; null once claimed.

cost_by_model.description: Tokens and attempts per model, priced when a card lists it.

cost_by_team.description: Tokens and attempts per docket team; `No team` for runs that name none.

cost_unpriced_attempts.description: Attempts whose model the rate card does not list, so not in `cost_usd`.

cost_usd.description:
Tokens priced by the rate card, plus the human minutes at its hour
rate. Absent without a rate card.

decided_alone.description:
Attempts with at least one escalation the agent's policy settled itself, and no
person was asked: a count apart from `decisions`, which only a person's answer makes.

decisions_answered.description: Decisions created in the window that a person has answered.

lights_off_rate.description:
Tasks merged in the window whose newest merged run began by itself and whose
requests never had a resolved decision, over the tasks merged in the window.

models.description:
Models the window's attempts named, and how many of them the rate card prices (none
without a card): the cost card says "N of M models priced" from this pair.

mrp_produced.description: Packs produced in the window and not yet reviewed.

oneOf.description: prill's figures; absent when `quality_unavailable` says why.

work_quality.description: How well the work came out: rates over the window's attempts, and the same cut by who did it.

Filter.description: What narrows an event trigger. Every field that is set must match.

after_seconds.description: For `change_set_waiting`: how long the change set waits before it counts, in seconds.

status.description: For an item event: the status the item is in after the event.

FinishedStep.description: A step that ended, with what it said.

assumptions.description: What the step took for granted.

ok.description: Whether the step ended well. Absent when the harness did not say.

questions.description: What the step left to the next one or to a person.

summary.description: What the step said it did.

tokens.description: The tokens the step used, cache reads not counted. Absent when not measured.

verdict.description: What a reviewing step decided, in the harness's own word, shown as data.

FolderCheck.description: What the folder check found at a path.

oneOf.description: The install command the checked-out commit's lockfile implies, when it has one.

import_closed.description: Include closed issues (default: false — only open issues are imported).

label_filter.description:
When non-empty, only issues that carry at least one of these labels
are imported; all others are skipped.

repo.description: Repository as "owner/repo" or a full GitHub URL.

token.description:
Personal access token. Optional — unauthenticated calls are allowed
but are rate-limited to 60 requests/hour.

GithubLinkBody.description:
Body of `PUT /api/items/{id}/github-link` and the response of
`GET /api/items/{id}/github-link` — the one new type this route family
needs.

repo.description:
"owner/repo" or a full GitHub URL — parsed the same way
`POST /api/projects/{id}/import-github` parses its own `repo` field.

HopKind.description: Whether a hop's latest event says it began or ended.

HumanMinutes.description:
Median and p90 of a human wait, in minutes. The start of each wait is
`viewed_at` when a human opened it, else `created_at`; the counts say which.

null_reason.description: `not_measured` when no row was resolved in the window.

start_created_at.description: Of those, waits that start at `created_at` (never viewed).

start_viewed_at.description: Of those, waits that start at `viewed_at`.

name.description: What the agent's comments and changes are signed with.

scopes.description: The projects and capabilities the credential holds.

IssuedCredential.description: A credential together with its secret, which is shown this once and never again.

item_type.description: A key of the project's type catalog (`Project::item_types`).

oneOf.description: Set: closing the task creates the next one.

recurrence_of.description: The closed task this one was created from by its recurrence.

oneOf.description:
The run dialog's Advanced values this task overrides (a JSON object),
or `None` when it follows the project.

source.description:
Sticky provenance marker for the prompt-injection
trust boundary: set once at creation time by whichever handler
created the item, and never mutated afterward — `UpdateItem` has no
`source` field, and the repository's item update has no code path
that writes this column, so an item's source can never change once
set. `#[serde(default)]` matters here: any JSON that predates this
field (an old export, or a hand-built import payload) deserializes
to [`ItemSource::default()`] (`Unknown`), which [`ItemSource::is_trusted`]
treats as untrusted — the same "unverifiable provenance resolves to
untrusted" rule migration 029 applies to pre-existing database rows.

source_artifact_id.description: The plan artifact this item was created from (`source` is `plan`), else `None`.

ItemBrief.description:
What "done" means for an item, typed so a verifier can check it.
`docs/contracts/brief-v1/` is its wire shape.

ItemBriefVersion.description:
One saved state of an item's brief. `brief_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the
brief-v1 JSON as the runner stages it (`brief.json`); it is empty for a
version recorded before hashes were kept.

created_by.description:
Who created the item through the API: `operator`, or the name of the agent credential.
`None` for an item made before callers were recorded, or by Tack itself.

merge_note.description: Why the task's last merge did not happen, while it has not; `None` once merged or never tried.

merged_by.description: How the newest merged attempt was merged: `button`, `done` or `auto`; `None` when nothing merged.

needs_review.description:
True when the latest finished attempt left a patch or a kept
workspace that nobody has reviewed yet.

node.description: A group when the item's type holds work or the item has children, otherwise work.

oneOf.description:
How far the work under a group is; `None` for work, for a group with no work under it, and
on a read that does not work it out.

started_by.description: `auto_start` when the newest request was started by the project's own rule, else `None`.

team.description: The docket team named by the newest request's resolved profile, else `None`.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the item through the API, in the same words as `created_by`.

ItemCard.description:
An item as the board and the item page show it: the [`Item`] plus what the run history says
about it. The extra fields are derived on read from executions and merges, never stored on the
item and never written back, which is why they are not part of the aggregate.

ItemDetail.description:
Detail envelope for `GET /api/items/{id}` — the item plus its assigned roles
and dependency edges.

ItemNode.description: An item of the tree, with how far the work under it is when it holds any.

oneOf.description: The position, in the change set's operations, of a `create` that makes the item.

ItemRef.description: An item an operation names: one the change set creates, or one the board already has.

ItemSource.description:
Where an item's title/description text came from. Backend for the
prompt-injection trust boundary: text imported from
GitHub Issues, Linear, or any bulk import is written by parties Tack
cannot vouch for, and becomes literal instructions to an autonomous
agent the moment the item is dispatched. [`is_trusted`](ItemSource::is_trusted)
is the single place that rule is encoded — nothing else in this codebase
should independently decide whether a `source` counts as trusted.

default_work.description: Exactly one per project, and it is work: what an item made without a type becomes.

ItemTypeLevel.description: Whether a type holds work or is work.

ItemTypeUse.description: A type with how many items use it, as the types route lists it.

Key.description:
The situation a notification is about, so the same situation is never open twice and the
fact that ends it can name it: `decision:<id>`, `run:<request>`, `change_set:<id>`,
`finished:<request>`, `due:<item>:<yyyy-mm-dd>`, `children:<parent>`, `memory:<project>:<team>:<entry>`,
`trend:<project>:<cut>:<name>`.

Kind.description: What happened that a person is told about.

LatestHop.description:
The step of a docket run an attempt is in, read from the text of its latest hop event so a
screen finds the step on the team's list without fetching the events.

cycle.description: The cycle a finished hop names; null when it names none (the first pass is not named).

role.description:
The role as the event names it (its first letter is upper case); match it to a team's
steps without regard to case.

verdict.description:
How the hop ended, in the event's words (`done` when it reported no verdict); null for a
hop that has started.

Level.description: How much a notification asks of a person.

api_key.description: Linear personal API key (create at https://linear.app/settings/api).

import_completed.description: Include completed/cancelled issues (default: false — open only).

label_filter.description:
When non-empty, only issues carrying at least one matching label are
imported; all others are skipped.

project_id.description:
Import only issues belonging to this Linear project ID.  Overrides
`team_id` when both are set.

team_id.description:
Import only issues from this team (slug or ID). When omitted, all
issues accessible to the key are fetched.

MeasurementSource.description: How a numeric usage figure was obtained.

Measurement_f64.description: A nullable metric paired with its provenance, avoiding fabricated zeros.

MemoryDecision.description: What a person decides about a memory entry that waits for them.

oneOf.description: What the harness saw that backs it, when it saw anything.

id.description: The harness's own id, which its commands take.

kind.description:
What sort of fact it is, in the harness's word (`generated`, `tool`, `pitfall`,
`convention`).

provenance.description: Where it was learnt, as the harness records it (the task, the date, the commit).

reason.description: Why the harness decided as it did, or why it waits.

stale.description: Whether what the entry names is gone since it was accepted.

subject.description: What it is about: a path, a label or a command.

MemoryEvidence.description: What backs an entry: the exit status of a command or whether a tool call succeeded.

reason.description:
Required when the attempt's pack recommends `reject` or the change altered how the work
is checked; a blank one counts as none.

MergedBy.description:
The merge that happened for an attempt: `trigger` is what asked for it
(`button`, `done`, `auto`), `merge_sha` the commit it landed on.

MergesByTrigger.description: Merges in the window, by what triggered them.

principal.description:
Who wrote it, as [`Principal::label`](crate::principal::Principal::label) says:
`operator:local`, `agent:<credential>`, `thread:<id>` for a reply.

Missing.description: One gap between a project file and what the computers report.

fix.description:
What the operator does to close the gap: docket's command for a team, the sentence that
installs an agent for a harness.

name.description: The team's name, or the agent's.

shape.description: A team's shape, when the file says it.

MissingKind.description: What kind of thing is missing.

ModelPrice.description: Dollars per million tokens of one model.

ModelProvenance.description:
What an execution request asked for vs. what an attempt ran on: both
model strings in full, and who named the served one (`reported`,
`requested` or `agent_default`).

requested.description: The model the request named; `null` when it named none.

served.description: The model the attempt ran on; `null` when nothing named one.

source.description:
Who named `served`: `reported` (the agent's own output), `requested`
(only the request) or `agent_default` (neither).

oneOf.description: The attempt's review; `null` until a person has given a verdict.

viewed_at.description: When the operator first opened the pack; `null` until then.

NobodyReason.description: Why nobody would take a card.

Node.description: What an item is for the screens: a group holds items, work is done.

Notification.description: A notice as the inbox keeps it.

failed.description: Deliveries given up on: refused for good, or still failing after the last try.

last_error.description: Why the newest failing delivery failed.

name.description: The channel's name, as the deliveries know it.

pending.description: Deliveries waiting for their first or next try.

open.description: How many notifications are open, whatever `limit` cut.

OpResult.description: What an applied operation did, in the words the plan's answer has always used.

item.description: The item a `create` made, or the one the operation changed.

moved_from.description: For a `move`, where the item was.

unknown_profile.description: The profile id that no profile has.

unknown_role.description: The role name the project does not have; the item has no role.

unknown_type.description: The type the project does not have; the item has the fallback type.

unresolved_team.description: The team that no profile, or more than one, names.

oneOf.description: Gives an item a role, a team's profile, or a profile: at least one.
`blocker` must finish before `blocked`.
A date, or `null` to clear it.
Puts an item under `parent`, or at the top when there is none.

OperationEdit.description: An operation to put in place of a waiting one.

Origin.description: Where a change set came from.

merged_not_reverted.description:
Merged and not reverted at the time of the query: no CI, defect or
window behind it, so it is not a quality figure (prill's `quality` is).

opened.description: Pull requests opened in the window, and what each is now.

Outline.description:
What `POST /api/projects/outline` and `POST /api/projects/{id}/outline`
read, as JSON or YAML. Unknown keys are refused rather than dropped, so a

fields.description: Custom fields of the project, by name (ADR 0022).

profiles.description: Agent profiles, by name; shared by every project of the board.

teams.description:

from it, and lists the ones no computer reports.

types.description:

ones it lacks and takes the names and colours of the ones it has.

depends_on.description: Items that must finish before this one, by `ref` or exact title.

estimate_unit.description: story_points, hours, days, or any other word as a custom unit.

software, web, mobile, construction, personal, homework, maintenance,

created.description: Items created (on a dry run, that would be created).

dependencies.description: Dependencies created between the new items.

items.description: The items in written order: parents before their children.

sections.description: What each section of a project file does, in the file's order; empty for a CSV.

warnings.description:

unpaginated match count so clients can render "N of M".

tasks_too_short.description: Recurring tasks with fewer runs, left out.

refs.description: Items, change sets and decisions the message is about.

How far the work under a group is, over every work item beneath it at any depth, hidden ones
excluded.

done.description: Work in a status of the workflow's done category.

ends.description: The latest due date of the work.

estimate_done.description: The estimates of the work that is done; `None` exactly when `estimate_total` is.

estimate_total.description: The estimates of all the work; `None` when no work under the group has one.

needs_you.description: Work that asks something of a person.

open_runs.description: Work with a run queued, running or waiting for a person.

starts.description: The earliest start of the work: when it started, else when it was created.

teams.description: Each team once, by name; work run by a single agent counts as a team named for the agent.

agents_on_board.description: How far an agent may go on this project: the rung and the caps on creates (ADR 0034).

auto_start_disabled_reason.description: Why auto-start switched itself off (the project dropped to L3); read, never written.

auto_start_max_open.description: How many runs the project keeps open at once on its own.

code_origin.description:
Where the project's code comes from; `repository` is a URL for

default_model.description:
The model a run uses when it names none and its agent is this
project's `default_harness`; changing the default agent clears it.

github_token_ref.description:
A `store:<name>` or `env:<VAR>` reference to a secret holding this
project's own GitHub token — never the token value itself (see
`tack_runner::secrets::SecretStore::resolve`). Resolved only
server-side, for the server's own outbound GitHub push/poll calls;
see `tack-api`'s `github_sync::github_token_for_project` for the

item_types.description:
The project's type catalog, in display order: served with the project so no screen
fetches it twice.

prepare_command.description:
How a run installs the project's dependencies: absent detects the command from the
lockfile, empty turns the install off, any other text replaces the detected command.

change_sets.description: Change sets with operations waiting for a person, the oldest first.

failed_runs.description: Runs that failed since the digest's `since`, the newest first.

items_by_status.description: The statuses that hold items, in the board's order.

waiting_on_person.description: What waits for a person, the longest wait first.

item_types.description: The item types a project made from the template starts with.

profiles.description: The agent profiles those roles use.

roles.description: The roles a project made from the template starts with.

teams.description: The teams the template expects its profiles to name; described, never created.

idempotency_key.description: The same key on a project answers the first change set again.

oneOf.description: Where it came from; absent means an MCP tool call.

origin_ref.description: The run or thread it came from.

reason.description: Why the change is wanted, in a sentence a person reads before deciding.

ProposedChangeSet.description: A change set as it stands after it was proposed.

applied_now.description: The positions of the operations that applied at once; the rest wait for a person.

made.description: False when the idempotency key had been used: this is the first answer again.

Quality.description: What prill measured. Present only when prill answered.

QuestionNoise.description: What one kind of agent asked a person, and how it went.

actions.description: Steps the agent reported in all, whatever it asked: what the rate is over.

granted.description: Answered with a go-ahead ÷ answered by a person.

harness.description: The agent; `Not recorded` when the run never named one.

per_100_actions.description: Questions of this kind per hundred steps; absent without a step.

as_of.description: The date the prices were read, as the operator wrote it.

models.description: Price per model string, exactly as a run names its model.

Ratio.description: A ratio with the counts it came from.

Recurrence.description: How often a task comes back once it is closed.

reason.description: Why the waiting operations are turned down.

RepositoryQuality.description: One repository's figures from prill's store.

cost_usd.description:
Tokens of the attempts that opened this repository's pull requests,
priced by the rate card. Absent without a card.

metrics.description: prill's `metrics/v1` document, as prill printed it.

qualified_per_usd.description:
prill's `qualified` ÷ `cost_usd`. Absent without a card, without a
`qualified` count, or when the cost is zero.

answer.description:
The answer as submitted (or as stored, on a replay), echoed back as
the operator sent it, extra keys included.

replayed.description:
`true` when this response is a byte-identical idempotent replay of an
already-committed resolution rather than a fresh write.

state.description:
Always `"resolved"` on a 200 — an expired/not-found/conflicting
decision is a distinct error response, never a 200 with a different
state string, so a caller need not switch on this field.

force.description: Override the "this device has newer work" guard.

key.description: Object key to restore. Defaults to the latest backup when omitted.

reason.description: Required to reject, optional to accept; a blank one counts as none.

agent_profile_id.description: The agent profile a task with this role runs with, when none is named.

Routed.description: The profile that would do one open card, and where it would run.

oneOf.description:
The ancestor the choice came from (an epic whose role or profile this item takes);
`null` when the item names its own.
Why nobody would take the card; `null` when someone would.

profile_id.description: The profile chosen; `null` when nobody would take the card and none is chosen.

role.description:
The role the profile came from; with `nobody` `role_without_profile`, the role that names
none.

source.description:
Where the choice came from: `run_settings` (chosen on the card), `role:<name>`,
`project_default`, `implementer` (the built-in profile, when nothing else is named) or
`ambiguous` (its roles name different profiles, so the project's default is used). An
item with nothing of its own takes the nearest ancestor's (`from` says which).

team.description:
The team the profile names; the card runs in it, or nobody takes it when no computer
reports it. `null` for a profile that names none: the card runs in its single agent.

RoutedFrom.description: The ancestor an item takes its profile from.

RunLimit.description: A run's token limit, who set it and who applies it, with the one sentence every screen prints.

enforced_by.description:
Who stops the run at the limit: `docket` stops the task itself; `claude-code` and
`opencode`: the runner stops the agent when its counted tokens reach it; `measured`: Tack
reads the agent's tokens and cannot stop it.

tokens.description: Absent when the run has no limit set in Tack.

used.description: What the run's latest attempt has counted so far, live while it runs; absent before any attempt.

RunOption.description: Whether one agent profile may run an item.

allowed.description: Any profile runs work; a group runs only with a profile that plans or researches.

node.description:
What the item is for running it: `group` (its type holds work, or items sit under it) or
`work`.

reason.description: Why the profile may not run it, in a sentence; `null` when it may.

RunSettings.description:
The run dialog's Advanced values a task overrides. Every field is optional;
a key this version does not know survives a round trip in `extra`.

approvals.description: A string, not an enum: the dialog validates it.

RungLevel.description: How far an agent may go on a project (ADR 0034, decision 4), in order.

RunnerSummary.description:
One row of `GET /api/runners` — every column `agent_runners` carries
(minus credential material — see `RunnerListingRow`'s own doc comment in
`tack-db`), plus its current fleet roster.

capability_snapshot.description:
Parsed `capability_snapshot` — see `labels`' doc comment for the
same "raw string always present" guarantee.

labels.description:
Parsed `labels` — `null` only if the stored value is somehow not
valid JSON (`labels_raw` always carries the raw stored string, so no
information is lost even then).

online.description:
Active, with a heartbeat inside the scheduler's window, as of this read.
Decided with `SchedulingPolicy::is_online`; never stored.

RunnerTimeCost.description:
Runner-observed wall-clock time cost — entirely different provenance
from the harness's self-reported [`Usage`]. `wall_clock_ms` is a fact the
runner/API directly witnesses (attempt start/end), never wrapped in a
[`Measurement`] since there is no "estimated" wall clock. No infra rate
is stored anywhere in this schema today, so `cost_usd_estimated` stays
`not_measured` unless a caller supplies `runner_rate_usd_per_hour`.

code.description:
One of the fifteen frozen `docs/contracts/runner-v1/errors/*.json`
codes (e.g. `not_found`, `conflict`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`invalid_transition`, `stale_lease`, `runner_revoked`).

details.description:
Per-code structured detail — shape documented per operation in
`docs/contracts/runner-v1/README.md` (e.g. `invalid_transition`'s
`{from, to}`, `stale_lease`'s `{attempt_id, current_fencing_token}`).

retryable.description:
Whether a conformant client may safely retry — derived from `code`
alone (`StableErrorCode::retryable`), never set independently.

RunnerV1ErrorEnvelope.description:
Documents `tack_protocol::execution::ProtocolErrorEnvelope`'s real wire shape
(`docs/contracts/runner-v1/errors/*.json`) for every operator
execution/fleet/runner/profile route — not `crate::openapi::ErrorEnvelope`,
a different, incompatible shape. A doc-only mirror, not a second runtime
authority: `tack-orch` must stay free of an OpenAPI dependency, so the
real type cannot derive `ToSchema` itself. Defined here rather than in
`crate::openapi` so this stays colocated with the routes it documents.
`code` is a free string, not an enum, for the same reason — its fifteen
frozen values are enumerated in `docs/contracts/runner-v1/README.md`.
Referenced only by *type* (utoipa's `ToSchema`), never constructed as a
value — real responses build the runtime type instead.

Weekdays and a time of day. `days` are ISO weekdays (1 Monday to 7 Sunday); the time is
the minute of the day in the zone `utc_offset_minutes` east of UTC names.

is then ignored.

StableErrorCode.description:
Stable error codes: the only values a client may branch on; error text and `details` remain
display and diagnostic data. The first fifteen are the runner-v1 contract
(`docs/contracts/runner-v1/errors/*.json`); the rest are the operator API's own, which the
runner routes never answer: one per rule the board enforces and one per failure of the HTTP
layer. The code decides the HTTP status ([`StableErrorCode::status`]) in one place.

reason.description: The code the run ended with, `ceiling` for a team's ceiling that sent no code, `cancelled`, or `unspecified`.

reported_at.description: When the board last heard what the team is doing; `null` when it never has.

runner.description: The runner whose report this is: the newest one when several report the team.

supported.description:
Whether the agent can say what its teams are doing. When `false`, `tasks` is empty and
`reason` says why.

tasks.description:
The tasks the team holds, the ones still going first. A task with `on_board` `null` is work
the board did not start: a person, a routine or another channel gave it to the team
directly. Tasks that ended stay for 14 days.

oneOf.description: Present with `needs_review`.

code.description: The code to send back as `accept`; it changes when the folder does.

commands.description: What the folder would run on the computer, one line each, as docket listed it.

tokens.description: The tokens the team may spend in the span; absent when the team has no limit.

used.description: The tokens it has spent in the span.

window.description:
How long the span lasts, in the harness's word for it (`none` for a span that never
restarts, `day`, `week`).

window_start.description: When the current span began; absent for a span that never restarts.

TeamDecides.description: Whether a team runs to the end alone.

TeamDelivers.description: What a team hands back when a task ends.

tasks.description: The work, what is going first and the queue after it.

profiles.description: The profiles that name the team.

`profiles` is `null`: the board knows the name and nothing else.

fix.description: What to change so the team runs lights-out; `null` for a team that already does.

profile.description: The Tack agent profile that names the team.

read_only.description:
The folders the team's sandbox reads besides its own work; `[]` for none, `null` when no
computer reports the team or its harness does not say.

records.description:
The record sets the team keeps and how many rows each holds; `null` when the harness does
not say.

works_in.description:
`repository` or `folder`; `null` when no computer reports the team or its harness does not
say. A folder team's work stays in its folder: nothing is merged.

can_propose.description:
Whether the member can propose items for a person to accept. Absent means the harness did
not say, which is not the same as `false`; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

model.description: The model the member runs on. Absent means the harness did not say.

reads_web.description:

team's network (`false`: it has none). Absent means the harness did not say, which is not
the same as `false`; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

role.description: What the member does, in the harness's own word for it, shown as data.

it reads none, or the harness did not say which.

writes_project.description:
Whether the member can change the project's files or run commands in it (`false`: it only
reads). Absent means the harness did not say, which is not the same as `false`; no field
may carry a harness's own key name.

What a team remembers about its work: the entries it has learnt and those that wait for a
person to approve them. Both lists are oldest first, as the harness gives them.

accepted.description: Checked or approved; the team reads them in its next task.

can_decide.description:

harness has its own command for it.

pending.description: Held back until a person decides; the team does not use them yet.

oneOf.description:
The team as the harness reports it now, with the entry no longer waiting; `null` when it
did not say.

runner.description: The runner that asked the harness.

default.description: Whether a task that names no method goes through this one.

error.description: Why the method cannot run at all: its file does not load. Absent for a method that loads.

The roles the method has a step for and the team has no member for: a task that names it is
refused. Empty when the team can run every step.

name.description: The name a task gives to choose it.

source.description: Where the team has it from, in the harness's own word, shown as data.

network and no member that reads the web.
The run proposes items, and no member of the team can.
The run changes the repository, and the team delivers a report or records.
The task names a method the team does not offer.

oneOf.description: The task names a method the team offers but lacks the members for: it would be refused.

steps_skipped.description: The task names a method the team offers but lacks the members for: it would be refused.

oneOf.description: The task names a method the team lists but whose file does not load.

method_broken.description: The task names a method the team lists but whose file does not load.

The team says one of its needs is not met, and that the work cannot go on without it (a
need that only degrades the work is a warning, not a misfit).

needs_unmet.description:
The team says one of its needs is not met, and that the work cannot go on without it (a
need that only degrades the work is a warning, not a misfit).

A need of a profile that the team it names says it cannot meet. A run that has one ends before
the team gets the task, because the team would stop and ask a person for what only its own
setup can give.

Whether the work cannot go on without it. `Some(false)` is a need whose absence only
degrades the work (a research team that cannot read PDFs): it is shown as a warning and
never refuses a run. Absent from a harness that does not say, which Tack reads as blocking.

fix.description: What the operator does to meet it.

kind.description:
What sort of need it is, in the harness's own word, shown as data; [`NEED_SIGN_IN`] and
[`NEED_MODEL`] are the two Tack's runner reports.

name.description: What is needed, as the team names it.

TeamNetwork.description: How far a team's agents can reach over the network.

TeamProfile.description: A profile that names a team.

misfits.description:
What the profile needs that the team says it cannot do; a run of it ends before the team
gets the task. Empty when the team meets every need, or did not say enough to tell.

TeamQueue.description: The work a team holds now.

waiting.description: Tasks that have not started or wait for a person.

TeamRecordSet.description: One set of records a team keeps.

TeamRecords.description: One set of records a team keeps.

rows.description: Rows in the set, whichever run wrote them.

its agent reports. Absent means the harness did not say, which is never the same as "none":
a screen shows what was reported and nothing it had to guess. No field may carry a harness's
own key name; a harness's own labels arrive only as data (`shape`).

harness did not say, which is not the same as no limit; no field may carry a harness's own

not say; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

`records` says. Absent means the harness did not say, which is not the same as a branch; no
field may carry a harness's own key name.

folder.description:
The folder a team that works in one writes in, as a path on the computer that runs it.
Absent for a team in a repository, or when the harness did not say; no field may carry a
harness's own key name.

members.description:
Who does the work: one entry per member, with the model it runs on. Absent means the
harness did not say; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

methods.description:
Every method a task may name, each with the roles the team lacks. Absent means the harness
did not say (an empty list is not a team without methods); no field may carry a harness's
own key name.

needs.description:
What the team's work still needs, each satisfied or not. Absent means the harness did not
say, which is not the same as needing nothing; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

oneOf.description:
How far the team's agents can reach over the network. Absent means the harness did not
say; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

Why the team claims no task now, when it does not: tasks sent to it wait. Absent means the
team is not paused, or the harness did not say; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

profile.description:
How closely a person supervises the team, as the harness names it (`attended`,
`lights-out`). Absent for a team of one, which has no such setting.

proposals_shared_across_tasks.description:
Whether what the members propose is kept for every task of the team together (`true`: a
name used in one task cannot be used again in another until the team's list of proposals
is recreated) or for each task apart (`false`). Absent means the team keeps no list of
proposals or the harness did not say; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

oneOf.description:
How much work the team holds now. Absent means the harness did not say; no field of this
type may carry a harness's own key name.

read_only.description:
The folders the team's sandbox may read besides its own work, as docket resolved them
(its machine-wide grants narrowed by the team's own setting); empty when there are none.
Absent when the harness did not say, which is not the same as none.

records.description:
The record sets the team keeps, with how many rows each holds. Absent when the harness
has no such thing or did not say.

shape.description:
A label the harness gives the team's shape, shown as it came and never sent anywhere.
Absent means the harness did not say; no field may carry a harness's own key
name.

steps.description:
The steps a task goes through, in order. Absent means the harness did not say (an empty
list is a team that reported no steps); no field may carry a harness's own
key name.

oneOf.description:
How the team reads the web, in the harness's own sentence: whether it does, why, and what
to change when it does not. Absent means the harness did not say, which is not the same as
no web; no field may carry a harness's own key name.

Whether the team works in a repository or in a plain folder. Absent when the harness did
not say, which is not the same as a repository.

TeamResumed.description: What a runner's harness said after it was asked to resume a team.

oneOf.description: The team as the harness reports it now; `null` when it did not say.

runner.description: The runner that asked the harness.

TeamStep.description: One step of the way a team handles a task.

oneOf.description: What decides the step passed. Absent means nothing checks it, or the harness did not say.

role.description:
Who does an `agent` step, in the harness's own word for it, shown as data. Absent for a
step nobody in the team does, or when the harness did not say.

sends_back_max.description: How many times it may go back. Absent means the harness did not say.

sends_back_to.description: The earlier step the work goes back to when the check fails. Absent means it goes nowhere.

project.description: The project the board started it for; `null` for work the board did not start.

oneOf.description: The step it is inside now.

task.description: The task's name in the team's own agent.

TeamToApply.description: One team to apply: a row of the import preview's `missing` list, or one of the file's `teams`.

accept.description:
The code docket gave for the commands the folder would run, once a person has read them:
the answer to an earlier `needs_review` for this team.

name.description: The team's name, which is also the name of its folder under `.docket/teams/`.

shape.description: The shape the team is made from: `build`, `respond`, `operate` or `routine`.

TeamViolation.description: One thing that makes a team need a person during a run, and how to fix it.

TeamWebRead.description: How a team reads the web and why.

fix.description: What the operator changes to give the team the web; empty unless the team reads none.

reason.description: Why the team reads as it does, a sentence the harness wrote.

TerminalReason.description:
Terminal reason from a runner attempt: `code`, `message`, and optional
`artifact`/`artifacts` on success; `workspace_kept_at` after a completed
recovery. The wire shape is fully documented by runner contracts; this
struct mirrors that contract, with a flattened `additional` field for
extensibility. All fields are optional; a fresh attempt carries no
`terminal_reason` until it reports one.

additionalProperties.description:
Additional fields not explicitly typed, preserved from the wire
(extensibility for future runner protocol versions).

last_message_at.description: The time of the latest message, or of the thread's creation when it has none.

profile.description: The agent profile whose runs are the thread's turns.

ThreadDetail.description: A thread with everything in it.

oneOf.description: One project: its digest, and nothing else.
The projects a credential reaches. `home` is the one project its turns run in.

Tokens.description: Tokens counted as the project's limits count them: cache reads are not part of them.

left_today.description: What is left of the day's limit; `null` without one.

limit_per_day.description: The day's limit; `null` when the project sets none.

per_run_limit.description: The limit of one run that sets none; `null` when off.

used_since.description: Used by the runs started since the digest's `since`.

Trigger.description: A rule that starts a run of a profile.

daily_cap.description: The most runs in a day (24 hours).

quiet_seconds.description: How long events must stay quiet before the run starts, in seconds.

scope.description: The project the runs happen in and, with a credential, the projects whose events count.

Turn.description: One run of the thread's profile, started by one message.

TypeColor.description: A colour by the design token it draws with, never a hex value.

auto_start.description: Whether the project starts tasks by itself; when it does not, no task is waiting for it.

by_reason.description: How many tasks wait for each reason, by code.

tasks.description: The tasks it would start and has not, most urgent first.

UpdateBackupSettings.description:
Incoming update. Any omitted/blank string field clears that override and
falls back to the environment default. A blank `secret_key` keeps the
existing stored secret (so the masked UI field can be left untouched).

retention.description:
Number of backups to keep. Must be at least 1 — `retention: 0` would
prune the backup that was just created (and, when it is the only one,
leave zero backups).

assignee.description: Omitted leaves the assignee untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

description.description: Omitted leaves the description untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

estimate.description: Omitted leaves the estimate untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

parent_id.description:
Omitted leaves the parent untouched; JSON `null` moves the item to the top. A group never
goes under work, the tree has at most five levels and no loops, and the parent must be in
the same project; a refusal is a 422 and writes nothing.

oneOf.description: Omitted leaves the recurrence untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

Omitted leaves the run settings untouched; JSON `null` clears them.
Anything but an object or `null` fails to deserialize.

default_work.description: `true` makes this the default work type; the previous one stops being it.

oneOf.description: Changes only while no item uses the type.

order.description: The position among the types, from 0.

delivers.description: Omitted leaves the line untouched; JSON `null` or an empty string clears it.

fleet_id.description: Omitted leaves the fleet untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

kind.description: What the profile does, from the same list as on create. A built-in profile keeps its own.

oneOf.description: Replaces the project's rung and the caps on creates; omitted leaves them.

auto_start_status.description: A status of the project's workflow; JSON `null` clears it.

default_model.description: Omitted leaves it untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

github_token_ref.description:
A plain `Option<String>`, not a double-`Option`, like every other
optional field on this DTO: an absent key leaves the stored
reference untouched. Since there is no `null` to spell "clear" with
here, clearing is done by sending the empty string, which the
repository (`tack_db::repo::projects::update_project`) stores as SQL
`NULL` rather than as a literal empty string.

prepare_command.description:
Omitted leaves it untouched; `null` detects the command from the lockfile, `""` turns the
install off, any other single line replaces the detected command.

repository.description:
Omitted leaves the field untouched; JSON `null` clears it. Same for
every double-`Option` field below.

agent_profile_id.description: Omitted leaves the profile untouched; JSON `null` clears it.

UpdateSprint.description:
A full replacement of a sprint's editable fields. Every field is written as
given, so an omitted `goal`, `start_date` or `end_date` clears the stored
value rather than leaving it alone — the edit form always sends all four,
and an empty box there means the user cleared it. `status` is not here: it
moves through its own route, which fires the lifecycle webhooks.

UpdateTrigger.description: What an edit changes; a field left out stays.

UsageEconomics.description:
Two independently-provenanced dollar dimensions, deliberately never
summed into one figure — see this module's doc comment.

model_token_cost_usd_estimated.description:
Pass-through of `Usage.cost_usd` — the harness/vendor's own
self-reported dollar figure, provenance (`measured` / `estimated` /
`not_measured`) preserved verbatim, never reinterpreted.

runner_time_cost.description: This module's own derived dimension — see [`RunnerTimeCost`].

attempts_unmeasured.description: Attempts counted above whose usage carries no token value.

implementation_tokens.description: Counted tokens (cache reads left out) of each request's first attempt (requests that are not rework).

rework_tokens.description:
Counted tokens of later attempts plus every attempt of a request whose
`metadata.rework_of` names another request.

verification_packs_unmeasured.description: Packs whose content is missing or does not carry token usage.

verification_tokens.description: Tokens in + out of every readable MRP's `usage`.

VerifierAgreement.description:
How often the verifier's word matched what became of the work. A task is *bad* when a person
rejected it or its pull request was reverted, and *good* when a person accepted it and it was
not reverted; any other task has no label and is not counted.

agreed.description: Said merge on good work, or reject on bad work.

false_approval_rate.description: False approvals ÷ bad work the verifier judged.

false_rejection_rate.description: False rejections ÷ good work the verifier judged.

handed_to_a_person.description: Labelled work the verifier handed to a person (`review`): neither right nor wrong.

verifier.description: Always `prill`: the pack Tack reads is the verifier's.

without_a_pack.description: Labelled work with no readable pack.

WaitKind.description: What a person is waited for to do.

WaitingBehind.description: One run that holds a slot of a full computer a queued request waits for.

question.description: The question the run waits for a person to answer; null when it waits for no one.

runs_at_a_time.description: How many runs the computer takes at a time.

started_at.description: When the run started, or was taken by the computer if it has not started (RFC 3339).

operations.description: How many of its operations wait.

WaitingReason.description: Why one task is not started.

text.description: The reason in a sentence, with the way out where there is one.

WaitsOn.description: What a waiting task waits for.

cuts.description: The success, first-pass and revert rates by each way of cutting the runs.

first_pass_acceptance.description: Tasks whose first attempt a person accepted ÷ tasks whose first attempt a person reviewed.

questions.description: Questions put to a person, by agent and kind.

revert_after_merge.description: Pull requests reverted ÷ pull requests merged or reverted.

rework_per_item.description: Attempts after a task's first ÷ tasks with an attempt. A value above 1 is more than one extra round per task.

stops.description: Runs that did not succeed, by the reason they gave.

success_rate.description: Runs that succeeded ÷ runs that ended after starting (failed or succeeded).

WorkflowConfig.description: Full workflow configuration for a project.

WorksIn.description: Where a team does its work.
